\subsection{12. Positioning implication}




The strongest positioning remains hybrid rather than purely game-dev:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Unity WebGL / Real-Time 3D Developer
Technical Visualization + Technical Art
XR / Simulation-adjacent portfolio
C# + shaders + optimization + 3D pipeline
\end{mdcode}




This market sample does not support relying only on “Unity Developer” as a generic title. The market is saturated with mobile/gameplay senior roles. Alexander’s differentiation should be technical visualization, WebGL, shader/view modes, optimization, CAD-to-web pipeline, and interactive inspection systems.

\subsection{16. Interpretation rules for future searches}

Rule & Reason \\

Do not assume “remote” means worldwide & Region restrictions are frequent \\
Separate LATAM-only from global remote & Colombia eligibility differs \\
Mark snippets separately & Snippets are not full postings \\
Do not infer salary & Most postings hide compensation \\
Check portfolio requirement manually & Often implied, not explicit \\
Record seniority exactly & Senior roles dominate this sample \\
Flag expired / talent-pool roles & Not all postings are immediate openings \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{17. Final market read}




The current sample shows a viable but narrow path. Generic Unity roles skew toward senior game development, mobile, and shipped-title experience. The best fit for Alexander is not a generic game programmer lane; it is a technical visualization / technical art lane where Unity, C\#, shaders, WebGL, optimization, Blender, and interactive 3D systems combine into one portfolio narrative.




The LATAM nearshore market is relevant, but small in this capture. The highest-value next step is not broad application volume. It is building a portfolio package that can satisfy the explicit expectations visible in Creamos, Mudtek, Flat2VR, Insight Global, and HyperVR: Unity proof, C\# proof, optimization proof, visual proof, and project documentation.
